classification.difficultyReason: Choose coordinates, derive boundary-line equations and use the intersection hint to locate distinct vertex types. The substantial additional decision is exploiting symmetry and finding an effective area partition of the octagon.

content.prompt:
A $1\times1$ square is drawn below. Eight lines connect the midpoint of each side to the two furthest vertices. What fraction of the square is taken up by the central octagon?

Hint: Each of the vertices of the octagon can be found as the intersection of two lines.

inlines.text: Find the vertices by intersecting the lines, then partition the octagon into a square and four triangles.

answer.worked:
Take the square's corners as $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, $(1,1)$ and $(0,1)$. Two upper-left boundary vertices are found from intersections:
$$\begin{align*}
2x&=\frac12x+\frac12\\
\frac32x&=\frac12\\
x&=\frac13\\
y&=2\left(\frac13\right)=\frac23
\end{align*}$$
This gives $(\frac13,\frac23)$. The leftmost vertex is found from:
$$\begin{align*}
2x&=1-2x\\
4x&=1\\
x&=\frac14\\
y&=2\left(\frac14\right)=\frac12.
\end{align*}$$
By symmetry, the eight vertices are $(\frac14,\frac12)$, $(\frac13,\frac13)$, $(\frac12,\frac14)$, $(\frac23,\frac13)$, $(\frac34,\frac12)$, $(\frac23,\frac23)$, $(\frac12,\frac34)$ and $(\frac13,\frac23)$.

Partition the octagon into the square with corners $(\frac13,\frac13)$, $(\frac23,\frac13)$, $(\frac23,\frac23)$ and $(\frac13,\frac23)$, and four congruent triangles. Each triangle has base $\frac13$ and perpendicular height $\frac13-\frac14=\frac1{12}$.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{octagon}}&=\left(\frac13\right)^2+4\left(\frac12\times\frac13\times\frac1{12}\right)\\
A_{\text{octagon}}&=\frac19+\frac1{18}\\
A_{\text{octagon}}&=\frac16.
\end{align*}$$
The unit square has area $1$, so the required fraction is $\frac16$.
